- [research/recovered/ad_small/reports/T017_BGM_PROPERTY_SEMANTICS.md:13](../../research/recovered/ad_small/reports/T017_BGM_PROPERTY_SEMANTICS.md?plain=1#L13-L13) — [CONFIRMED-TARGET] Spot BGM resolves key `bgm` via `0x597A20 -> 0x4693F0`. `0x4693F0` constructs `bgm@<variant>`, asks `0x464290` whether that property exists across the structure/super chain, and if present returns it through `0x4647D0`; only when absent does it request base `bgm`. Thus a qualified `@` suppresses base fallback, and a child/base `@` found by `0x4647D0` suppresses parent fallback.
- [research/recovered/ad_small/reports/T017_BGM_PROPERTY_SEMANTICS.md:14](../../research/recovered/ad_small/reports/T017_BGM_PROPERTY_SEMANTICS.md?plain=1#L14-L14) — [CONFIRMED-TARGET] `0x4647D0` returns a found field by copying node string `+4` and scalar `+0x20` unchanged. It does not normalize RHS `@` to empty. In the battle spot branch, `0x48F3CE -> 0x597A20` copies that string; `0x48F443` tests its length and any non-empty value goes to `0x4BDE40` at `0x48F473`. Therefore `bgm=@` reaches the normal audio resolver as literal `@`, not empty string. With no `@` audio asset, it follows the ordinary missing-name resolver/reset semantics. This is analogous in outcome, but not representation, to an explicit no-BGM marker.
